The test image shows a corn ear with:
- Healthy yellow kernels at the base
- Pink/salmon-brown discolored, shrunken/rotted kernels concentrated at the **tip** of the ear
- Dark discoloration at the very tip/silk end
- No green or white mold visible

This tip-based infection strongly suggests Gibberella or Fusarium ear rot. Let me check reference images.
The Gibberella reference shows mostly stalk/husk symptoms. The Fusarium reference shows scattered kernel decay. Let me check Diplodia for comparison.

**Analysis:**

The test image shows:
- Corn ear with **healthy yellow kernels at the base**
- **Pink/salmon-brown, shrunken, rotted kernels concentrated at the tip** (silk end)
- Dark discoloration at the very tip
- No white mold covering all kernels (rules out Diplodia), no green mold (rules out Trichoderma/Aspergillus), no scattered starburst pattern (rules out Fusarium)

**Key distinguishing features:**
- **Tip-based infection**: The rot progresses from the silk channel inward — classic Gibberella pattern
- **Pink/reddish-brown discoloration** of affected kernels matches "pinkish-white mold at ear tip" with "pink to red kernel streaking"
- Diplodia starts at the **base**, Fusarium is **scattered**, Aspergillus is **olive-green** — all ruled out
- The Gibberella description explicitly notes: "Fusarium ear rot — mold on scattered or clustered kernels **rather than starting at the tip** as in Gibberella ear rot"
